Definition: separate, i.e. consecrated (as prince, a Nazirite); hence (figuratively from the latter) an unpruned vine (like an unshorn Nazirite)
BiblicalUsage: Joseph is called separate from his brethren in his father's blessing, and the law lays out the vow of the Nazarite, separated to the LORD. Samson is to be a Nazarite from the womb, and Amos says God raised up young men for Nazarites in Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Nazarite shows what a life set apart looks like: unshorn, undrunk, and untouched by death, a man whose very hair says he belongs to God. Samson's strength was never in the hair itself, but in the separation it marked.
